summary: Democratic Gov. Janet Mills was term-limited, so the seat was open. Hannah Pingree (Democrat) won a three-way race against Bobby Charles (Republican) and Rick Bennett (independent).

candidates.name: Hannah Pingree
candidates.bio: Hannah Pingree is a former Speaker of the Maine House (2008-2010) and former director of the Governor's Office of Policy Innovation and the Future.

positions.summary: Says she would invest $100 million a year in affordable housing and double the homestead exemption for Maine homeowners.
Says she would create a state-backed public health insurance option that employers can offer and lower prescription drug costs through bulk purchasing.
Says she would offer free, full-day Pre-K to every 4-year-old whose family wants it and raise the minimum teacher starting salary to $50,000.
Says she would reach 100% clean energy by 2040 through competitive auctions for local solar, wind and storage.
Says she would ensure access to the full range of reproductive health care, including rural maternity care.

candidates.name: Bobby Charles
candidates.bio: Bobby Charles is a lawyer and former U.S. Assistant Secretary of State.

positions.summary: Says he would abolish the state income tax, cut regulations, and create a $100K homestead exemption for property tax relief.
Says he would dismantle cartel networks operating in Maine and enforce strict public safety and immigration policies.
Says he wants schools refocused on reading, math and science, with educational freedom and curriculum transparency for parents.
Says his energy plan would cut energy costs for Mainers and restore reliable, affordable power.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called)
